equities.name: TSX Composite
equities.commentary: The TSX Composite closed at 32,427 on March 31, gaining 1.54% on the day as reports of potential US-Iran negotiations drove energy and risk-sensitive sectors higher.1 The index declined approximately 6% over the full month of March, reflecting elevated uncertainty from Middle East supply disruption and the February employment loss of 84,000 jobs.2 Energy sub-indices posted the largest monthly gains within the TSX, consistent with WTI crude's advance above $100/bbl, while materials underperformed amid gold's 14% monthly decline. The database tracks 727 Alberta projects — the province most directly exposed to TSX energy sector performance — and 364 mining projects with direct materials sector linkage.3

equities.name: S&P 500
equities.commentary: The S&P 500 closed at approximately 6,496 on March 31, rising 2.40% on the day, though the index remained approximately 9.4% below its January 2026 peak on a closing basis.4 March was characterized by elevated volatility driven by Middle East geopolitical developments and the Strait of Hormuz supply disruption; the March 31 advance followed reports that the US government is considering diplomatic resolution to the Iranian standoff.5

equities.name: DJIA
equities.commentary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at approximately 46,117 on March 31, advancing approximately 2.0% on the day alongside the broader US market rally.6 Blue-chip industrials with Canadian supply chain exposure — including steel and energy equipment names — tracked the energy sector's advance as WTI moved above $100/bbl.

equities.name: Nasdaq Composite
equities.commentary: The Nasdaq Composite closed at approximately 21,469 on March 31, the largest percentage advance among major US indices at 3.24% on the day.7 Technology-linked names outperformed on the expectation that diplomatic resolution of the Hormuz crisis would reduce input cost pressure on data centre and grid electrification projects; the database tracks 18 telecom and data infrastructure projects in Canada with US market linkages.
